scores.evidence: if GitHub is down, nothing new deploys, but running workloads aren't affected (Argo keeps the last applied state)
scores.rationale: Claims about OIDC federation, keyless cosign signing, Argo CD pull semantics, PreSync hooks, Kyverno audit/enforce modes, Renovate minimumReleaseAge and ECR immutability are all accurate, including the subtle areas (fork-PR trust, expand/contract rollback safety).

scores.evidence: The real critical path is migration throughput, not platform features. Building the platform takes roughly 10 weeks. Moving 50 services... 5–7 months
scores.rationale: Directly answers the sequencing request, resolves unspecified constraints with stated defaults, excludes scope explicitly with reasons, and the schedule is credible for the assumed team.

scores.evidence: System of record for desired state in each environment... Exactly one writer path per environment
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, data ownership and trust boundaries are stated per component and honored everywhere, including break-glass reconciling back to git; no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: Run an expand-style migration via the chart's migration Job in staging. Deploy, then revert... Run the old app against the new schema.
scores.rationale: Time-boxed spikes test the riskiest assumptions before commitment, each with explicit results that change the plan, plus fixture harness, timed rollback drills, load tests before waves, and a continuous production canary.

scores.evidence: all targets are assumptions until confirmed... Impact if wrong | How and when it's checked
scores.rationale: Every design-bearing assumption is explicit with sensitivity (what changes if wrong) and a confirmation date; numbers are consistently labeled as estimates to verify.

scores.evidence: The v1.5.0 tag is withdrawn... the other 45 services never see v1.5.0
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures—bad template fan-out, unsafe migration rollback, CI compromise, GitHub outage, duplicate promotes (idempotency), fork-PR abuse—each with concrete detection, containment and recovery; only flaky-test erosion is unaddressed.

scores.evidence: Alerts on symptoms, each linked to a runbook... platform-canary hasn't reached dev in 60 minutes
scores.rationale: Ownership split, business-hours on-call sized to a 4–5 person team, meaningful health signals, rehearsed break-glass and rollback, and migration/rollback paths for every change are all concrete.

scores.evidence: Runner minutes: about 150–250k a month... Check against current GitHub pricing before you budget.
scores.rationale: Identifies the dominant cost driver with a stated volume basis, scaling behavior, concrete controls (caching, concurrency cancel, budget alert) and a costed hosted-vs-self-hosted tradeoff with a revisit trigger.

scores.evidence: Reversibility | ... Hard. It sets the trust model and what every team does day to day.
scores.rationale: Each decision carries an explicit reversibility rating and revisit trigger; the genuinely hard commitments (GitOps trust model, legacy shutdown) get early validation and archived fallbacks, while easy choices are made quickly.

scores.evidence: Deferred item | Trigger to build it
scores.rationale: Uses existing tools throughout, defers preview environments, Backstage, multi-region and contract testing with explicit build triggers, and lists M1 stubs so simplicity doesn't drop essentials.

scores.evidence: T3... A workflow in the pilot repo pushes an image with no stored secrets. The same workflow run from a branch or another repo is denied
scores.rationale: Tasks T1–T13 have concrete done-when criteria, dependency-justified ordering, day-1 first steps, and each spike states exactly which result would change the plan and how.

checklist.evidence: Build the service inventory with columns: service, owner team, tier, stack + build tool, current CI... Escape hatch: a pre-build/post-test hook input
Add ci.yml running alongside the legacy pipeline, build-only. Compare test results and image contents for one week.

Third-party actions pinned by SHA... signs keyless with cosign... Kyverno checks the signature when pods are admitted
This is safe only if the migration was additive (expand/contract...). Spike S1 tests whether that holds.
Contract testing between services | Integration breakages between services found in staging more than twice a month
Per-PR preview environments | Repeated staging contention or teams asking for them after M4
PR checks p95 under 10 minutes... Docker layer cache goes to ECR with cache-to type=registry... Path filters.

Prod: PR needing approval from the service's CODEOWNERS... Git history is the audit trail.
